service.name: pfactory
service.title: PFactory
service.description: Governed planning grounded in live cloud/Backstage context. A planning session is ingested from an idea or spec, enriched with org/cloud context, decomposed, and scored by four review gates (architecture, security, best-practices, feasibility) that each return 0-1 with citations. A human approves, then PFactory emits governed GitHub issues and sets the RFC-0001 correlation key.

skills.name: plan-create
skills.description: Start a governed planning session from an idea or a spec. Give it a title, a description and the target repo; it returns a session id you use for every later step. This is the front of the PARR funnel: nothing reaches AIFactory without a plan.

skills.name: plan-enrich
skills.description: Pull live cloud and Backstage context into an existing planning session, so the plan is grounded in the org's real infrastructure and catalog rather than in guesses.

skills.name: plan-review
skills.description: Run the four review gates over a session: architecture, security, best-practices and feasibility. Each returns a 0-1 score with the citations behind it, so a low score can be argued with rather than merely obeyed.

skills.name: plan-approve
skills.description: Record the human governance decision on a reviewed session (approve or reject, with an optional note). PFactory will not emit work without it.

skills.name: plan-emit
skills.description: Emit the approved plan as governed GitHub issues and set the RFC-0001 correlation key that threads the work across AIFactory, TFactory and CFactory. Use this when a plan is signed off and ready to build.

skills.name: cloud-discover
skills.description: Run a read-only cloud posture assessment of an AWS, Azure or GCP account: enumerate resources, detect misconfigurations with Prowler (CIS/OCSF), build a service-topology diagram, and emit an accept/flag/reject verdict into findings/. Nothing is mutated.
